profile.name: Terrisa Bukovinac
profile.bio: Terrisa Bukovinac is an anti-abortion activist who founded Pro-Life San Francisco in 2017 and the Progressive Anti-Abortion Uprising in 2021, and served as president of Democrats for Life of America starting in 2020. She ran in the 2024 Democratic presidential primary, receiving about 2.7% of the vote in New Jersey. She is running as an independent in New Jersey's 9th district.

platform.point: Makes ending abortion the center of her campaign, describing it as genocide.
Presents resisting fascism as her second main campaign theme.
Advocates a federal abortion ban, defunding Planned Parenthood and repealing the FACE Act.
Supports lowering the cost of childbirth and expanding parental leave.

liberty.evidence: On abortion, supports a federal ban, fetal personhood and repealing the FACE Act; no stated positions found on drugs, LGBTQ rights, guns or speech.

profile.notes: The liberty score rests on abortion alone, since no other social positions were found. The Commons portrait is described as a campaign picture, so it was not used.

profile.name: Lynn Chapman
profile.bio: Lynn Chapman is the Independent American Party candidate for Nevada's 2nd congressional district.
profile.notes: No campaign website or issue statements were found; only the state candidate filing list confirms the candidacy.

profile.name: Gonzalo Duran
profile.current_role: Vice chair of the Bronx Conservative Party
profile.bio: Gonzalo Duran is a military veteran and founder of Devil Dog USA, which helps veterans move into civilian life. He is vice chair of the Bronx Conservative Party and a district leader for the 79th Assembly District, having left the Democratic Party in 2023. He previously ran for Congress in NY-15 in 2024.

platform.point: Restore accountability, personal responsibility and economic opportunity in the Bronx, and oppose socialism.
Support veterans, including those affected by burn pit exposure.
Lists public safety among his core campaign issues.
Lists housing, employment and transportation as campaign priorities for the Bronx.

profile.notes: His campaign site lists issue areas without detailed positions, so no domains are scored.

profile.name: Blay Tarnoff
profile.bio: Blay Tarnoff is the Libertarian Party candidate for New York's 4th Congressional District in 2026. No further biographical details were found in the sources checked.
profile.notes: Ballotpedia could not be retrieved and no campaign site or coverage was found, so the profile is minimal.

profile.name: Priscilla Ghaznavi
profile.bio: Priscilla Ghaznavi is running for New York's 7th congressional district on the Our Future line as an independent. Born in Washington, D.C., she has lived in New York for over 30 years and has worked in business and creative leadership roles at several publicly traded companies.

platform.point: Promotes accountable, results-driven leadership that links opportunity and access.
Emphasizes greater public participation in government.
Stresses community organizing and advocacy as a basis for her work.

profile.notes: Campaign site describes general themes rather than specific policies; no domains scored.

profile.name: Nathan Weise
profile.bio: Nathan Weise is the Libertarian Party of Ohio's listed candidate for Ohio's 1st Congressional District in 2026. No further public biographical information was found.
profile.notes: Listed by the Libertarian Party of Ohio (https://lpo.org/candidates/); he appears to have replaced withdrawn Libertarian John Hancock, which is unconfirmed.

profile.name: Thomas McMasters
profile.bio: Thomas McMasters served as mayor of Huber Heights, Ohio, from 2014 to 2018. He ran for Ohio's 10th congressional district as an independent in 2016 and is the Libertarian nominee for the seat in 2026.

platform.point: Focuses on finding inefficiencies in government and reducing wasteful spending.
Says he scrutinizes bill language to catch wording that undermines how a law works in practice.
Says he draws on ideas from across different political philosophies.

profile.notes: No campaign website or detailed issue positions found; Ballotpedia could not be reached.

profile.name: Brennan Barrington
profile.bio: Brennan Barrington is an engineer with a bachelor's degree in aeronautical and astronautical engineering from Ohio State University. He is the Libertarian nominee for Ohio's 15th congressional district in 2026 and has not held elected office.

platform.point: Wants to sharply reduce the scope of the federal government and return authority to states and individuals.
Seeks to eliminate regulations he views as deterring success and expanding bureaucracy.
Favors reforming taxes along Georgist land-value and Pigouvian lines.

economy.evidence: Calls for shrinking the federal government and eliminating regulatory systems, while rejecting socialism.

profile.notes: No campaign website found; bio and positions come from the Libertarian Party of Ohio candidate page.
